evidence.reason: MEASURED at baaf1e44b27a0006ab6316b75383fe88b3856e01 (main, clean). scripts/write_verification_record.py takes --command, --exit-code and --summary as caller-supplied arguments and executes only git rev-parse to fill repo_commit when none is given; it runs none of the commands it records. The present writer's behaviour does not establish that every historical record was produced through it. All 39 VERIFY records are VERIFY v1 attributed testimony: each carries recorded_by and repo_commit, and all 154 commands[] entries across them carry only command, exit_code and summary. Some VERIFY records cite retained outputs and their SHA-256 digests, including VERIFY-20260821-0001 and VERIFY-20260915-0001; these references do not constitute a standard per-command observed-execution contract. No contract exists that binds, per command, machine-captured stdout and stderr, the execution environment, the verifier version or content hash, the test or rule version, the property the command is relied on to establish, and a verifier lineage status. SELF_MODEL_SCHEMA.md states this directly: VERIFY v1 records are attributed testimony about execution evidence and do not independently execute commands, and a future v2 writer should run commands, capture exit code and output, bind results to repo HEAD and write the record itself; no gap, plan or decision records that deficiency or schedules that writer. ABS-0004 Section 4.17 defines VerificationRun (verifier executor reference, verifier version, rule or test version, content-addressed inputs, execution environment, result, verifier_lineage_status) as defined and deferred. The tree contains no GitHub Actions workflow (there is no .github directory), and the sources examined contain no evidence that any check is configured to require verification bound to the exact candidate before merge. External CI and manual checks are not excluded by that absence. The self-model pre-commit hook checks staged self-model records in clones where scripts/hooks/install.sh has been run; core.hooksPath is unset in the packaging executor's clone at this commit. This gap records an absence of an observed-execution contract, not that any recorded result is false.

name: VERIFY records are attributed testimony of execution rather than observed execution, and no recorded check is required against the exact candidate before merge
notes: Origin: the 2026-11-23 automation programme recorded in GAP-0005. Its step 2, evidence production, has no gap of its own; the reviewing executor confirmed against the repository that the deficiency is distinct from the catalog, ancestry and authorization gaps and recommended a separate record.

Ordering constraint stated by the reviewing executor and adopted: verification must exist for the exact candidate before the decision that relies on it. A record written after merge cannot supply acceptance evidence that did not exist before the merge.

Historical VERIFY v1 records keep their standing as attributed testimony. Producing observed-execution records must not convert any earlier record into observed execution, retroactively or by association.

Relations: GAP-0005's first slice, the C7 implementer and verifier pair, is to be carried on the records this gap produces; C10's verifier-lineage check depends on GAP-0008 and is not supplied by this gap, which can record the verifier's identity and content hash but cannot by itself establish independence. Observed execution narrows what a record can misstate about a run; it does not establish that the commands run test the property they are relied on for (P2), which remains a per-command declaration.
This gap authorizes nothing. Automation of plan admission, merge, or any delegated decision is outside it.
recommended_first_slice: A v2 VERIFY writer that executes the declared commands itself rather than accepting their results as arguments: in a clean checkout of one exact commit, refusing a dirty tree or a commit mismatch; per command, retaining the stdout and stderr bytes under a durable reference with their content digests, and recording the exit code and the property the command is declared to establish; recording the environment (interpreter version, dependency set digest, platform), the writer's own content hash as verifier version, the versions or content digests of the tests, rules and other effective inputs the commands ran, and the verifier executor reference; and leaving verifier_lineage_status at the weakest value its evidence supports rather than defaulting it upward. Paired with a CI workflow that runs the same writer on the candidate merge commit of a pull request before merge and retains the record, with the workflow's own configuration declared as an effective input per the Section 4.7 tool-configuration disclosure constraint. If the candidate changes after the record is produced, the record no longer covers it and any acceptance condition relying on it is re-evaluated. Mapped onto the Section 4.17 fields without implementing the deferred IndependenceAssessment. Falsified before reliance: a caller cannot inject an exit code; a failing command yields a failing record; a dirty tree and a commit mismatch are refused; altering the retained output bytes after recording is detected as a mismatch between their recomputed digest and the recorded one. A re-run is a separate record; two runs are compared only on explicitly declared properties, and byte equality is expected only where the command's output contract requires it, since timing, timestamps and other nondeterministic output can differ without indicating that either record is corrupt. v1 writer and records unchanged.
risk: VERIFY v1 does not supply a standard per-command contract binding observed execution, retained output, environment, and verifier and test versions, and no recorded check is required against the exact candidate before merge. Automated acceptance relying on v1 testimony alone could mistake reported success for observed success. The C7 and C10 evidence required by the GAP-0005 programme must preserve this distinction when per-step operator review is removed.
summary: VERIFY v1 records state which commands were run and with what exit codes, as reported by the recording executor; the current writer executes none of them. No standard contract binds, per command, machine-captured output, environment, verifier and test versions and the property established; some records cite retained outputs and their digests, which does not supply that contract. The repository defines no GitHub Actions workflow, and no recorded check is required against the exact candidate before merge. Observed-execution verification is a prerequisite for any delegated or automated acceptance, and the VerificationRun record it needs is defined in ABS-0004 Section 4.17 and deferred.
